reasons: Hard-coded local API address for the docs link.
Continue to Export is enabled before validation is run.
The quick tour popup referenced by the script is missing from this file.
No automated tests are visible for the page.

sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Page setup and header
sections.what: Sets the page title and style link, then shows the app name and an API status badge that starts at Checking.
sections.why: The badge tells the user whether the backend is reachable.
sections.watch_out: If the script fails to load, the badge stays at Checking forever.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Welcome screen with six journey cards
sections.what: Opens the content area and shows the step 0 welcome screen with a hero heading and six cards describing upload, goals, planning, review, validation and export.
sections.why: Gives users an overview of the whole process before they start.
sections.watch_out: Card numbers and titles are typed by hand, so adding or reordering a step means editing each card.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Feature list and start button
sections.what: Lists platform features and a Start button that calls startWorkflow, plus a link to the API docs and a link to the classic interface.
sections.why: Likely reason: an introduction for first-time users.
sections.watch_out: The docs link points to localhost on port 8000, so it fails on any other server. Feature claims like 25 plus models are fixed text.

sections.name: File setup (part 4)
sections.title: Document upload form
sections.what: Form to choose a document type, audience, and one or more TXT, MD, CSV, or JSON files, which is sent to handleFileUpload. Also has a result area and a list of uploaded documents.
sections.why: Lets users add reference material before planning.
sections.watch_out: The file type filter only works in the browser. The server must also check file types.

sections.name: File setup (part 5)
sections.title: Step 1 navigation buttons
sections.what: Back, Continue, and Skip buttons for the knowledge base step.
sections.why: Uploading documents is optional, so users can skip.
sections.watch_out: Skip and Continue both call nextStep, so skipping records nothing about whether documents were uploaded.

sections.name: File setup (part 6)
sections.title: Survey planning form
sections.what: Form for research goal, audience, model type, and must-include topics, sent to handlePlanSurvey. Below it is a result panel with download and accept buttons.
sections.why: Collects what the AI needs to draft a survey plan.
sections.watch_out: The result panel stays hidden until a plan is generated, so its buttons cannot be used before then. The audience list here differs from the upload form.

sections.name: File setup (part 7)
sections.title: Review, validate, and export screens
sections.what: Review step with a container the script fills, a validation step with an info list and a Run Validation button, and an export step.
sections.why: Groups the remaining workflow steps into the page.
sections.watch_out: Continue to Export is not disabled in the HTML, so it can be clicked before validation runs.

sections.name: File setup (part 8)
sections.title: Export cards, loading screen, and script
sections.what: Three export cards, a completion message, a Start New Survey button, a full-screen loading overlay hidden at first, and the script tag that loads wizard-app.js at the end.
sections.why: Likely reason: loading the script last lets the page draw before the script runs.
sections.watch_out: The overlay is hidden with an inline style, so if the script stops early it may never hide and block the page.

summary: The main page of the survey wizard, with six steps from welcome to export.
purpose: Lets a user build a survey by moving through knowledge base upload, planning, review, validation, and export.
why: A single page with hidden step panels keeps the whole flow in the browser without page reloads.
how: The page shows a progress bar and one step panel at a time. Buttons call functions in wizard-app.js. Results from the backend are placed into empty containers.
inputs: User entries in the upload form and planning form, and uploaded files.
outputs: Visible screens, and the actions passed to wizard-app.js such as uploading documents, planning, validating, and exporting.
risks: Some links point to a fixed local address. The Continue to Export button is clickable before validation. The quick tour popup it calls is not present in this file.
debug: If a button does nothing, check that its function name matches one in wizard-app.js and that the browser console shows no error. If a step does not show, check its id and the active class.
